subject: Post-incident: ClearStream production slowdown — RCA & next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@clearstream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T01:15:22Z
Subject: Re: Production slowdown — initial update

Samantha — quick update from our side after initial mitigation.

What we saw: starting 2026-11-04 00:42 UTC a subset of requests to your Dedicated pool began experiencing degraded tail latency (~3-6s spikes) for synchronous generation calls. The control plane remained up; inference nodes were accepting traffic but token-emission stalled when certain cached KV entries were loaded.

Immediate action taken: we throttled new long-sequence requests to your pool, moved critical traffic to a warmed replica, and increased continuous-batch sizes to reduce scheduling jitter. Incident detection and mitigation prevented data loss.

I will follow up tomorrow with a full RCA and timeline. Apologies for the disruption — we know these spikes impact your user experience.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

---
Note: logs attached (query-sample-logs-20261104.txt) for your ops team to review.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@clearstream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T10:05:00Z
Subject: Full RCA: 2026-11-04 ClearStream production slowdown — timeline, root cause, action items

Hi Samantha — as promised, attached is a concise RCA and timeline ("rca_clearstream_20261105.pdf"). Summary below; full document linked at the bottom.

Executive summary
- Impact: 2026-11-04 00:42–01:12 UTC — intermittent high tail latency for RPCs routed to your Dedicated GPU pool; ~18% of requests saw >2.5s latency, ~4% >4s. No token loss or model corruption.
- Root cause: a regression in a cache eviction heuristic in the inference runtime combined with an atypical request pattern from a set of long-context batch jobs. The heuristic produced a pathological KV-cache churn that blocked background GC on two GPUs, causing token emission stalls.
- Mitigation: we shifted traffic to pre-warmed pool replicas, applied a runtime hotfix to revert the heuristic, and restarted two affected nodes.

Timeline (high level)
- 00:42 UTC: first latency alerts from your synthetic monitors and our internal SLO alarms.
- 00:45 UTC: on-call engaged, began packet capture and KV cache inspection.
- 00:52 UTC: confirmed GPU-side stall correlated with cache GC spikes.
- 01:04 UTC: traffic reroute to warmed replicas completed.
- 01:12 UTC: token emission returned to baseline; monitoring showed degradation cleared.

Customer-visible impact and scope
- Affected workload: synchronous generation calls with prompt lengths >3k tokens and heavy prefix sharing.
- Your traffic: ~7% of your requests matched the pattern; estimated user-facing error/timeout rate increased by ~1.1% during the window.

Action items (Redwood) — committed
1) Runtime fix: revert eviction heuristic + add safety guard to prevent GC stalls — deployed 2026-11-05 09:20 UTC. (Owner: Runtime team)
2) Automated canary: add dedicated canaries that exercise long-context prefix sharing to detect this pattern earlier. (Owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-12-02)
3) Pool resilience: add secondary warm-replica capacity by default on Dedicated pools with >150 qps. (Owner: Infra, ETA: 2026-12-16)
4) Customer lens: we'll run a traffic replay against a mirrored pool to quantify any unseen failures and share results with you. (Owner: Account Reliability, ETA: 2026-11-12)

Requested actions (ClearStream)
- If possible, share one anonymized prompt set exhibiting long shared prefixes or the job IDs so we can reproduce locally. We noted some pattern markers in the attached logs.

SLA and credits
- We're evaluating the event against your SLA. Per our standard process we will propose a credit if the incident qualifies. I will loop in Billing with a formal credit notice by 2026-11-09.

Next steps
- Proposal: 30-minute technical walkthrough this Friday 2026-11-06 15:00 PT to review playback and answer ops questions. Please confirm availability or suggest an alternate.

Attachments: rca_clearstream_20261105.pdf, query-sample-logs-20261104.txt

Link to full report: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cRCAClearStreamRCA

Thanks again for your patience — we take these incidents seriously and are doubling down on detection and resilience improvements.

— Jonas

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@clearstream.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:05:12Z
Subject: Re: Full RCA: 2026-11-04 ClearStream production slowdown — timeline, root cause, action items

Jonas — thanks for the thorough RCA and the quick fix. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

1) Can you confirm whether any tokens or user inputs were persisted incorrectly or if there was any chance of partial responses being cached and later returned to other sessions? Our compliance team is anxious about cross-request contamination.

2) For SLA credits — roughly how will you calculate the credit amount and timing? We need this for our finance review.

We can do the 11/06 15:00 PT call. Please send an invite.

— Samantha
Samantha Lee
VP Engineering, ClearStream Payments

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T13:27:45Z
Subject: Internal: ClearStream questions — tokens, credits, and customer call prep

Marissa / Lauren — copying the external thread above for context. Samantha asked two things we should resolve before the Friday call: (A) contamination question for compliance, (B) SLA credit estimate.

Proposed quick answers:
- Contamination: our investigation shows no evidence of cross-request KV leakage. The stall prevented emission but state was not promoted across request boundaries; runtime invariants protect per-request KV. We should get SRE/runtime to sign off with a short paragraph and a log excerpt that proves no KV flushes occurred across connections. (Action: Marissa — can you get that sign-off and a one-paragraph ready note?)
- Credits: Katie in Billing will need the exact window and impacted RPS; propose a provisional credit calculation: prorated monthly usage for the affected qps * 1.5x per our precedent for degraded QoS events. (Action: Lauren — can you confirm precedent and ping Billing for a formal calculation?)

I'll book the call and include runtime + SRE. If there are other asks we should surface them now so we can prepare artifacts.

— Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@clearstream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T17:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Full RCA: 2026-11-04 ClearStream production slowdown — timeline, root cause, action items

Samantha — quick follow-up with answers to your questions and the calendar invite attached.

1) Contamination/compliance: confirmed — no cross-request persistence or contamination. Attached log excerpts show per-connection KV namespaces remained isolated and no promotion of transient entries occurred. The runtime team will present a 5-minute verification on the call.

2) SLA credits: Lauren has drafted a provisional credit estimate and Billing will produce a formal credit memo by 2026-11-09. Expect a credit equal to the prorated usage for the impacted window with a 1.5x multiplier per standard degraded-service precedent; final number after Billing review.

Call: 2026-11-06 15:00 PT (invite sent). Agenda: brief playback, verification from runtime, credit process, and action item ownership.

Attachments: rca_clearstream_20261105.pdf (again), verification-excerpt.txt

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

— Jonas
